correctness.rationale: Theorem (rt=34 exact) independently reproduced bit-for-bit: a=(1,2,3,4,0,0,5,6) is one-cluster with unique cycle {0,1,2,3,4} (5->0,6->5,7->6); b=(1,7,3,4,0,2,5,6) is a permutation; |w|=34; direct simulation collapses all 8 states to {0} with first-reset prefix 34. Fresh independent BFS (integer-mask, separate code path from verifier) gives forward distance 34 with 248/256 masks reachable and reverse distance 34 (255 ancestors), matching stored dist_main.json entry-for-entry (248 entries, FULL=0, singleton {0}=34). Pair-automaton BFS confirms all 28 unordered pairs merge (synchronizing). All 10 catalog entries re-checked with fresh BFS: each resets as claimed, each BFS distance equals claimed L, each a one-cluster 5-cycle, each b a permutation. Enumeration claims reproduced: 320/512 assignments keep one-cluster 5-cycle property; orbit computation under 5-cycle rotation + S3 on {5,6,7} yields exactly the 14 listed canonical a-types (orbit sizes 5+4x15+7x30+15+30=320). Proposition (perm-b max=34) fully reproduced by independent exhaustive rerun of all 14x40320=564480 automata in ~32s: total sync 550796 exactly as claimed, per-type sync 39168 (type0), 39468 (0,0,5,5), 39452 (0,0,5,6) all match, global max 34 attained uniquely by the main witness, first-12 total 471876 matches. Draft honestly distinguishes proof (exact BFS + exhaustive perm census) from heuristic evidence (484k mixed trials + 318k ILS kicks finding nothing >34, correctly not claimed as proof of full-slice M). Minor rounding only: 550796/564480=97.5758% vs stated 97.55%, 477625/484000=98.6829% vs 98.67% — immaterial.

originality.rationale: Checked the conjunction: (i) existence of binary 8-state synchronizing DFA with one-cluster letter a of 5-cycle type and exact shortest reset length 34 via explicit a=(1,2,3,4,0,0,5,6), b=(1,7,3,4,0,2,5,6) 8-cycle, w=aaabaabaaaabaabaaaabaabaaaabaabaaa to {0} with minimality; (ii) exact perm-b sub-slice maximum 34 uniquely attained over 14 canonical a-types x 40320 b (564480 automata, 550796 sync). Live retrieval on two services (Crossref + arXiv API/abs/HTML) with 7 queries (exact claim, prime-cycle one-cluster, reset-34/n=8, extremal reset) found only universal upper bounds and disjoint exhaustive programs. Steinberg full text proves only <=(n-1)^2 (=49 for n=8) with no lower-bound example and no n=8 specialization; Beal et al. prove O(n^2) upper bound only; Kisielewicz-Szykula 1404.3311 proves refined D*(m,k) upper bounds and a sieving algorithm (tables for m=4..12, savings for n=7/n=6) with no (n=8,k=5) census; Experiments verifies <=49 for all binary n<=12 but publishes no slice maximum; Extremal Properties gives ternary n^2-3n+3 series, structurally disjoint (binary vs ternary, circular/Cerny vs one-cluster 5-cycle, series vs finite census). Targeted reset-34/n=8 searches returned only irrelevant physics/ML hits (e.g. superconductors, continual learning) or chaos-synchronization papers, i.e. null result for the exact constant. Hypotheses, quantifiers (universal bound vs existential exact witness + universal-exhaustive perm-subslice max), parameter ranges (all n vs fixed n=8,k=5,perm-b), constants (49/28 vs exact 34), and scope (inequality proof vs 256-subset BFS certificate + 564480-case enumeration) are all disjoint. No source covers or implies M>=34 or perm-max=34.

value.rationale: Independently worth finding later. Not textbook: Cerny open since 1964, exact small-n maxima for structured slices are active research. Not parameter substitution: 5-cycle one-cluster restriction is qualitative (Steinberg theorem regime, excludes 8-cycle Cerny shape, changes combinatorics), not n=7->8. Not tiny epsilon gain: 34 exceeds the aperiodic universal bound 28 by 6 (21% over) and attains ~69% of Cerny 49, proving prime-cycle restriction still permits super-aperiodic slowness — a regime-crossing threshold with landscape meaning between 28 and 49. Not unexplained enumeration: every catalog entry carries shortest word + forward/reverse BFS distances + replay check, plus distribution histograms (mixed 484k, perm 564k) and comparison to Steinberg/Cerny/aperiodic bounds; exhaustive perm-b census (564480 automata, exact max 34) is a complete enumerative theorem for a natural subcase (permutation letter), with reusable stdlib verifier (<2s). Fallback anticipated >=25 catalog if >=32 missed; actual 34 exceeds the motivating >=32 threshold. Honest scope (full M not pinned, non-perm >34 possible) preserves value as lower bound + benchmark.
